scope: Sternicza 11 optional basement garage and MG Cyberster AWD clearance

vehicle.model: MG Cyberster 77 kWh AWD, Polish specification for production years 2024–2025
notes: The Polish laden clearance is the baseline. Precise lowest-point location and measurement load distribution are not published.
Overhangs are corroborated by the Finnish manufacturer diagram and the 77 kWh 4 WD manufacturer manual for another market; verify the actual vehicle.
The Finnish diagram gives a 2691 mm wheelbase, 1 mm different from Poland. The model uses 2690 mm;955+2690+890=4535 mm.
The other-market manual's 106.7 mm minimum AWD clearance has no explicit load condition and does not replace Poland's 105.6 mm laden value.
Nominal tyre radii are calculated from size markings, not measured loaded rolling radii.
MG Poland says AWD operates only in forward travel. Geometric fit does not assess traction or reversing uphill.

siteEvidence.livingFloorStatus: Existing adjustable model assumption, not a measured level
notes: The straight alignment uses the full mapped street-boundary-to-facade distance, which differs slightly from the minimum setback.
Street-entry elevation is interpolated from the existing terrain grid, not a kerb or footway survey.
Basement clear height, slab/floor build-up, openings, internal walls and foundations are unmeasured.
When enabled, a proposed vehicle gate relocates into line with the basement; it is not an existing-access survey.

modelAssumptions: Quasi-static straight-line traversal, excluding suspension dynamics, braking pitch, crossfall, steering sweep and traction.
Conservative flat underside at the chosen ground clearance over the complete car length, including unmeasured bumpers.
30mm additional reserve is an editable planning allowance, not an MG requirement.
Interior ramp continuation consumes real basement length and reduces entrance headroom beneath the fixed slab.
Door and convertible-roof opening envelopes remain unverified.
Drainage is illustrated flush. Any real raised threshold, kerb or gate track needs inclusion in a measured detailed profile.
Waterproofing, structural alterations, groundwater, drainage capacity and street access remain project-design matters.
The candidate's 2.00 m inside continuation consists of 1.60 m of curved lower transition and a 0.40 m flat apron. The remaining flat bay includes that apron.
Closed-car overhead passage uses an assumed 3.20 m wide by 2.10 m high clear door opening, separate from the 2.30 m floor-to-slab height. Door hardware and opening envelopes are not verified.

legalBenchmark.status: Former WT benchmark; transitional applicability to confirm
notes: ELI records repeal of the former 2002 Technical Conditions regulation on 2026-09-21.
Act 31 July 2026, Dz.U.2026/1161 introduced Building LawArticle 102 a, an 18-month transitional route from 2026-09-20 for specified submissions after an investor declaration.
Former§70 explicitly gives 25% for individual garages. This is not a vehicle approach/breakover approval.
Former§14(1) gives 3 m access width. The 2.7 m ramp provision in§103(2) expressly addresses garages above 25 cars per level.
Former§102 provides garage/door dimensions and drainage before underground entry;§107 describes floor drainage and a 30 mm containment edge.
The 2023 amendment to§12(6)(1) includes a 1.5 m boundary setback for ramps with specified exceptions; a road plot has a separate exception.
WR-D-33 v 01.5 is voluntary ministry guidance for the public-road connection. Confirm road reserve/footway levels; do not automatically subtract a universal 5 m landing from the private forecourt.
No parcel-specific MPZP permission, structural feasibility or construction approval is established.
